evaluations.label: A
errors: The opening describes accommodating 'approximately 15 to 18 people.' There are 15 people; approximately 18 refers to available office positions before allocating a room to the lounge.

The outline says professor–assistant sharing is 'common in other faculties but not necessarily here.' This reverses the discussion: André describes sharing as an implicit tradition within their school, while Susan says professors in other faculties have their own offices.

'Action Items: (none)' contradicts explicit commitments: André will investigate room separation, additional desks in three-person rooms, and possible placement of Gisella with other school administrators; Susan will ask Maggie and Pierrette; attendees will bring preferences or proposals.
Minor naming inaccuracies: 'Unimile' should be Unimail, and the summary's 'Gisela' is rendered Gisella in the transcript.
strengths: Captures the room types, furniture requirements, shared equipment, and basic staffing/capacity figures in the body.
Identifies important open questions about partitioning, four-person capacity, lounge functions, and professors' preferences.
Correctly records the follow-up meeting for next Tuesday at 2 p.m. and the existence of another allocation proposal.
weaknesses: The empty action section and unexplained numbered speaker labels make responsibility difficult to establish, although some next steps appear elsewhere.
Omits the agreement that everyone needs an individual desk and understates the group's movement away from project-based seating.

Does not clearly capture Susan's own-office preference, Martin's willingness to share with a noise-tolerant colleague, or the proposed investigation of placing Gisella with another school administrator.
Repeats material between the summary and outline without adding enough operational detail.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Minor naming inaccuracies: 'Andrei' should be Andre, 'UniMile' should be Unimail, and 'Gisela' is rendered Gisella in the transcript.
strengths: Clearly distinguishes fixed room count from open assignments and explicitly states that no final layout was chosen.
Accurately explains the 15 people, approximately 18 positions, and reduction to 16 positions if a two-person room becomes the lounge.
Preserves important distinctions: everyone gets an individual desk, part-time attendance reduces simultaneous occupancy, Martin can share despite frequent calls, and Susan needs confidentiality.
Correctly assigns the room-separation investigation to André and consultation with Maggie and Pierrette to Susan.
Concise, logically organized, and appropriately cautious about project grouping and the lounge's unresolved function.
weaknesses: Omits André's additional investigations into fitting four desks in a three-person room and placing Gisella with another school administrator.
The attendee-wide task of bringing preferences or sketches appears in the body but is absent from the action checklist.
Describes the next meeting as merely 'discussed'; the participants actually agreed on next Tuesday around 2 p.m.
Omits David's preference for sharing with other assistants, although it captures the more consequential privacy and desk constraints.

evaluations.label: C
errors: Assigns follow-up with Maggie and Pierrette to Andrei. Susan explicitly volunteers to ask them at 30:54.
Lists distributing configuration documents as an outstanding action. Documents were distributed or confirmed available during the meeting.

Says splitting rooms is 'currently not feasible due to building and security regulations.' André only tentatively thinks the answer is no and commits to checking; no confirmed prohibition or feasibility determination was reported.

Says part-time schedules 'reduce desk demand' and that growth requires visitors or temporary staff to 'share existing desks.' The group explicitly agrees that each person needs their own desk; part-time attendance reduces simultaneous room occupancy, not individual desk requirements.

The general summary says proposals will be merged with the other group's proposal before next Tuesday's review. André says they will merge them when the other proposal is available; that deadline was not established.
Lists scheduling the next meeting as a future action even though next Tuesday around 2 p.m. was agreed during the meeting.

'Management recognizes this as a priority' introduces an institutional endorsement of the lounge that was not stated. Participants discussed expressed demand and previous discussions, while its exact purpose remained open.
The office-space description is cited at 00:06, before the supplied transcript begins. André's presentation starts at 00:54.
Minor naming inaccuracies: 'Andrei' should be Andre, 'Unimile' should be Unimail, and 'Gisela' is rendered Gisella in the transcript.
strengths: Broad coverage of capacity, privacy, administrative noise, visitors, project grouping, equipment, smoking rules, and coffee facilities.
Includes André's investigations into room separation, four desks in three-person rooms, and possible administrative placement outside the allocated offices.
Recognizes the need for absent colleagues' input, informal proposals, and comparison with another planning group's solution.
Explains the limited visitor capacity and why moving provides an improvement without eliminating future space pressure.
weaknesses: Incorrect ownership of the Maggie/Pierrette consultation could send follow-up to the wrong person and leave Susan's commitment untracked.
Mixes completed work, agreed arrangements, tentative possibilities, and genuine outstanding actions.
Repeated sections amplify unsupported conclusions about desk sharing and room modifications.
Extensive repetition makes the reliable decisions and assignments harder to find than in B or D.

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Shared space with another group' implies an additional occupying group. The transcript establishes another group developing an allocation proposal, not a separate group assigned to share the offices.
'Room splitting ... ruled out for now' overstates the status. André tentatively suspects the answer is no and promises to investigate; there was no verified ruling.
Lists scheduling the follow-up as an outstanding next step, although the participants agreed to next Tuesday around 2 p.m.
Minor naming inaccuracies: 'Andrei' should be Andre, 'Unimile' should be Unimail, and 'Gisela' is rendered Gisella in the transcript.
strengths: Compact and readable while covering most consequential constraints and open questions.
Correctly captures individual desks, the benefit of part-time attendance, Susan's confidentiality needs, and Martin's willingness to share.
Includes all major follow-up topics: room separation, an extra desk in three-person rooms, alternative administrative placement, absent colleagues' preferences, and attendee proposals.
Explains the lounge's capacity cost and competing reading, meeting, and visitor functions, alongside available coffee facilities.
weaknesses: Does not name action owners: André owns the three feasibility investigations, and Susan owns consultation with Maggie and Pierrette.
Does not explicitly state that the room count is fixed or that this meeting produced no final allocation.
Presents a visitor slot in Gisella's office without the important qualification that senior visiting researchers were considered unsuitable there; exchange students or interns remained possible.
Some wording is more categorical than the discussion, particularly around rejected strategies and the strength of support for lounge arrangements.

rationale: Overall scores are the arithmetic mean of the four equally weighted criteria. B is the most reliable and actionable, with careful treatment of open decisions and correct ownership of its listed actions. D is concise and broadly complete but omits owners and overstates some tentative conclusions. C covers the most material, but incorrect ownership, unsupported feasibility claims, and desk-sharing contradictions substantially reduce reliability. A captures the broad discussion but misses important constraints and follow-ups, incorrectly reports no action items, and reverses the comparison with other faculties.
